newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes costly, draw marginal interest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes costly, draw marginal interest.

text.p: U.S. refiners were moderately interested in foreign crudes Tuesday, opting for alternative domestic grades due to the prohibitive import arbitrage.
North Sea sellers, however, were still seen attempting to move prompt Brent cargoes to the U.S., with one European trader offering a 300,000 barrel parcel.
The cargo was offered at Dec West Texas Intermediate plus 15 cents cif, amid relatively thin supply of other North Sea grades and minimal discussion in the foreign market.
Unconfirmed reports persisted, meanwhile, that one million barrels for mid-Dec had sold recently to a U.S. Gulf refiner.
Traders insisted that the narrow 50-cent WTI/Brent spread for December, and 70-cent January spread, was uneconomic.
Some demand was noted for regional light, sweets like Cusiana, being bid at WTI plus $1.00 cif for late December.
A cargo for Dec 16-20 was offered around a 45-cent premium against WTI fob, but some said the price was "too rich".
Colombia's state Ecopetrol also tendered to sell South Blend crude for delivery on the Pacific side of the country before Dec 10.
Prices were notionally pegged at $2.70 a barrel fob discount against WTI.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a full cargo of Dec Brent traded at $22.60 a barrel, about 20 cents below the IPE close. Two partials also traded at $22.60 a barrel.
Intermonth Brent spreads were weaker, but none were dealt.
Dec/Jan Brent was assessed at 28/31 cents, down from 29/32 cents during the London session.
